articles.body:
Final Fantasy Resonance is essentially an adaptation and reimagining of the mobile game Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, with a rich story, dozens of cameos, and turn-based RPG combat without the gacha mechanics of the original. IGN's Final Fantasy Resonance guide will help you master the combat, find every collectible, and fight every boss with ease.

articles.body:
Prime Video originally launched in 2006 as Amazon Unbox in the U.S. and underwent a series of name changes as the years progressed. It wasn't until later in 2011 that the service became a part of the Amazon Prime subscription rather than an add-on for it. Now in 2026 everyone with access to an Amazon Prime subscription will also be able to watch movies and shows via Prime Video as an added membership benefit . You can still pay for a separate Prime Video subscription separately if you choose to.

In addition to being a streaming service, Prime Video is also a VOD platform that lets you rent and buy movies digitally.

The cost of Prime Video is baked into an Amazon Prime membership, but you can also choose to pay for just Prime Video separately. Within that, you can choose to pay for the base subscription with ads or add an additional monthly fee to go ad-free. Amazon also offers the choice to make monthly payments or pay an annual subscription price for a slight discount, however, the upgrade to ad-free is only available as a monthly payment of $4.99 as of the April 2026 price increase .

While there isn't a free trial available for a standalone Prime Video subscription, there are a couple of Amazon Prime free trials available that can get you access. There's the standard 30-day free trial of the service as well as 6-month free trial available for young adults. Both options waive the subscription fee but will automatically start payments as soon as the trial period is over.

In addition to the base Prime Video subscription, you can also choose to add on other streaming services to the same monthly bill.

Amazon's Prime Video service has a wide variety of movies ant TV shows available at any given time, but it is most known for its original content. You can check out the full collection of Amazon Originals directly from the Prime Video website or see what's coming in November 2026 .

articles.title: All 99 Tablet Shard Locations - Final Fantasy Resonance Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Tablet Shards are the main collectibles in Final Fantasy Resonance. They are found scattered across the world and are spotted by a golden glitter on the
articles.body:
Tablet Shards are the main collectibles in Final Fantasy Resonance . They are found scattered across the world and are spotted by a golden glitter on the ground. Some are pretty easy to find, while others are quite hidden. This guide lists all 99 Tablet Shard locations in Final Fantasy Resonance and the rewards you unlock for finding them .

After collecting a few, you can go to the Oblivion Palace and obtain rewards based on the number of Tablet Shards you have gathered.

This guide is written as a walkthrough, so you can follow it from the start to find every Tablet Shard in the main story as you progress. We have also split them up by the earliest chapter in which they can be found. However, since they aren't numbered in-game, tracking down specific missing ones can be tricky. We recommend keeping this guide open and using it throughout your playthrough.

All 99 Tablet Shards in Final Fantasy Resonance

Click on a link below to jump to that section of this guide.

There are 12 Tablet Shards to be found in Chapter 1.

The Tablet Shard is found by some crates behind the Equipment Shop Clerk.

On the left side of the pool of water in the southwest of town.

Go to the northernmost house and hug the left wall to find a hidden path. Head up the ladder and interact with the glittering spot to the left.

Behind some greenish equipment once you climb down the first set of stairs and change areas.

After the bridge breaks and you climb back up, head back toward where you fell to find this shard behind a broken pillar.

Behind the first barrel on the dock to the south.

Underneath the tree left of the Equipment Shop.

The Cavern of Swords is located in the desert near Grandport Harbor, north of Marauder Cave. Once inside, the shard is behind a rock near the middle of the cave.

If that stupid Chimera is giving you a hard time, there's no shame in running away or using a Smoke Bomb.

Immediately after entering, go up the small staircase and turn left to find it on the floor.

At the top of the stairs, just before fighting Tap to Reveal . On the right side of the passageway heading north.

On top of a higher platform after fighting Tap to Reveal . Hard to miss because it's on the main path.

You will find 15 Tablet Shards in Chapter 2.

Dilmagia, the Machinopolis Tablet Shard 1

Just left of the entrance, behind an orange barrel.

Dilmagia, the Machinopolis Tablet Shard 2

Behind some crates in the direction of the weapon shop.

Dilmagia, the Machinopolis Tablet Shard 3

After meeting Lid, take the left stairs up and go all the way to the end of the platform.

Dilmagia, the Machinopolis Tablet Shard 4

Still in the shipyard, take the right stairs down and grab this shard near a metal beam.

When first entering Mt. Thunderclap, don't pay Lid for the easy-peasy shortcut. Instead, follow the path and you'll eventually spot the Tablet Shard on the floor to your right.

You can get this Tablet Shard in two ways. The first is to pay Lid, unlock the shortcut, then follow the path to find the shard beside a tree.

The second way is to not pay Lid and proceed through Mt. Gagazet until you reach the world map. Halfway towards the Dwarven Forge, take the east path once you find a sign to get back on Mt. Gagazet. Keep going until you find the stairs and drop down to reach the shard.

Tip: We suggest the second way to both save gil and grab another Tablet Shard on the way.

As stated above, you can return to Mt. Gagazet from another entrance. Once inside, keep going until you reach a small slope. The Tablet Shard is hidden under a rock after descending the slope.

From the Weapon Shop, head all the way left, down, then cross a bridge to spot the shard on the floor at the end of the platform.

After speaking to Borin for the first time, head down the large staircase toward the monster. Instead of facing it outright, go south to grab this shard.

After entering, walk all the way left to find it on the floor.

After taking the first elevator up, go east into a fenced area. Take the ladder farther east, and then west to find this shard.

Once you activate the second elevator and take it up, go north, ignore the stairs going down, and look to the left of a container on the upper platform for this shard.

After calling the elevator by the entrance, don't go up yet. Grab the shard behind the pillar first.

After riding some platforms, you'll eventually come to a staircase leading up in the northeast section. Look to the right of the stairs to spot the Tablet Shard.

Shortly after the previous Tablet Shard, you'll ride a platform to the center of the area. Look behind the pillar on the left to find this one.

Chapter 3 contains 15 more Tablet Shards.

Immediately after entering the city, go right and find this shard next to the sailor.

Just above the fountain with the two statues in the middle of the city, by the northwest benches. Next to the quest NPC if it's your first time in the city.

On the long bridge in the northeast of the city, between some flower pots.

After getting on the boat, follow the path around to the northeast. This Tablet Shard is to the left of the entrance to the next room.

Besides the staircase leading to the entrance, pretty much on your way.

After you return to the Cave of Waters on your way to Lake Dorr, go up the first ladder and you'll see the Tablet Shard on the floor.

This Tablet Shard is beside the first ladder you come across.

After meeting Tap to Reveal again, continue left through Waterfall Way and you'll eventually spot it on the floor in the room filled with waterfalls.

Continue along the path, and you'll spot a Tablet Shard between waterfalls. Cross the wooden bridges, go up, and then turn left to reach it.

Just south of the Weapon Shop, next to a well.

North of the Item Shop, next to a thin tree.

After lowering the water for the second time and opening the way to the north, look to the left side of Leviathan's statue for this one.

Eventually, you'll reach another area where you need to lower the water. When you hop on the boat, go north to the ladder and grab the Tablet Shard on the right before climbing it.

After you lower the main area's water level, the dungeon will lead you to a set of stairs and then a ladder. After you climb down a ladder, the shard will be within reach.

Prepare to find more 16 Tablet Shards in Chapter 4.

On the ground to the left of the Item Shop.

Near the eastern entrance, by a trash can.

Once you reach Zoldaad and read the gazette, you'll learn the colosseum has been rebuilt. If you fancy some rewards, travel back to Grandshelt and go west from the plaza to find the colosseum area. Keep going west on the ground floor to find the Tablet Shard near some barrels.

Zoldaad, The Imperial Capital Tablet Shard 1

Go to the Castle Plaza and grab this Tablet Shard on the ground to the right of the fountain.

Zoldaad, The Imperial Capital Tablet Shard 2

Travel to the Residential District to spot this one in the bottom right corner.

Zoldaad, The Imperial Capital Tablet Shard 3

Once you hit the slums, this Tablet Shard is near some crates.

After entering the Underground Tunnel, follow the path right and down a small set of stairs. Keep going east until the path splits into east and south. Go south and through the metal gate to find the Tablet Shard on the other side.

From the second save point, go north and hugh to the right wall to find a hidden staircase leading to this Tablet Shard.

Go around the right side of Jake's house and then turn left to find a hidden passageway against the back wall. Go up the ladder and the Tablet Shard will be right below you.

Behind a metal pillar in the northeast section.

From the entrance, head up the ladder to the left of the save point. Walk right, and you'll see three switches. Hit the first switch three times. Then cross the platforms to reach the westernmost platform to grab this Tablet Shard.

From the entrance, head left past the save point and go up when you reach the end. Follow the stairs and the path around, and you'll reach a switch on your left. Activate it, and it'll move a metal platform you can walk across. Once you do, the Tablet Shard will be on your left.

After you get the Master Key, go south into the next room. The Tablet Shard is inside the first cell to the right.

With the Master Key in hand, return to the room you were locked in. To get there, go east from the second save point and then all the way south. Unlock the door with the Beefy Man and grab the Tablet Shard near him.

Speak to the Beefy Man after unlocking his cell to receive an X-Potion and a Mist Ether.

At the bottom of the stairs leading to the throne room, there are two horse statues. Look behind the left one to find the Tablet Shard.

Go right of the throne room door and the save point and enter the first room you see. There's an exclamation mark inside the room. The Tablet Shard is in the bottom-right corner.

You'll find 17 more Tablet Shards in Chapter 5.

From Chapter 5 on, we have an airship to call ours, which means world exploration is open. To keep this guide in order, we will tackle objectives by their in-game recommended level, while still prioritizing side content over the main story.

From the entrance, go down the stairs on the right to find the shard hiding behind the White Mage.

Directly in front of the Armor Shop, behind a crate.

By the waterfall in the center of the city, on the right side behind a pillar. To get there, use a teleport stone to warp to the Storefront, then go west into the blue portal.

By the entrance, near some wooden barrels and crates.

On the far east side of the village, there's an igloo and a snowman. The shard is next to Olaf.

Left of the first save point, sitting next to a fallen pillar.

Near the second save point, on the left staircase next to a fallen chandelier.

Immediately left of the entrance, among the desks.

In the Forbidden Wing, go up the ladder near the save point and then all the way east.

To the left of the giant locked door, up against the chain.

In the large forest clearing, west of the camp. The Tablet Shard is at the end of this single road.

In a patterned tile near the entrance, before the stairs.

In the middle of the way as you climb the stairs.

To the right of the stairs immediately after coming back inside from the snowy outer ring.

In a snowpatch after the Azure Pot enemy, near the elevator.

Available on your second visit to Fina's Psyche. On the east side of the camp, behind some boxes.

Chapter 6 harbors 12 more Tablet Shards.

In the destroyed office where you first encounter the teleporter, the shard is between two desks on the right.

In the room where you activate a teleporter by activating three computers. The shard is on the catwalk in the bottom-right corner.

In the teleporter-filled room east of the entrance. Once you climb the ladder, grab the Tablet Shard in the right girder.

By a tree left of the entrance save point.

Top left side of the big square area, east of the second save point.

To the right of the shop, behind the waterfall.

In the right corner of the second room, before the stairs.

Descend the west stairs to proceed within the shrine. Once down, take the narrow path to the east, then climb the nearby staircase to grab this Tablet Shard near a broken pillar.

After climbing down a ladder, go immediately west and climb up another ladder. The Tablet Shard is to the south once you're up.

Once you reach the Yakhanati boss room, the one where the camera perspective changes to horizontal, go east of the stele to find a hidden room. Climb the stairs and then the ladder to find this Tablet Shard.

In the room with many elevators, just keep going to find the Tablet Shard on your path.

There are 8 Tablet Shards to be found in Chapter 7:

Right of the item shop, under the tree by the bridge.

After the first bridge, go west and down the slope to find this Tablet Shard.

Pretty much on your way as you go south from one bridge to another.

In the left side of the area, beneath a tree.

Along the main path, north of the save point.

In the path south of the second save point, resting by a rock.

In the second area from the entrance, along the main path, the Tablet Shard will be cozily tucked on the right side before you make a slight turn west.

Just after the cutscene, the Tablet Shard will be glinting there, calling for you. If you missed it the first time for any reason, it's south of the second save point.

The last 5 Tablet Shards are here in Chapter 8:

You can access Dragon's Maw all the way back in Chapter 5, but since its recommended level is 55, the same as the last dungeon, it's pretty much a tell that you should only brave it in Chapter 8.

Midway through the dungeon, you'll face a Magitek boss. Once you defeat it, grab the Tablet Shard where the machine stood.

From the entrance, go right up the stairs when the path allows.

Still in the first area, proceed until the path splits, then go west to find this Tablet Shard.

Once you reach the room with invisible floors, keep going until the path splits, then take the west one to find the last, number 99, Tablet Shard at the end.

The Oblivion Palace can be found as soon as you get your Chocobo. Go south from the village of Kol, cross the quicksand, and once you spot a sign indicating that Felicitas is to the east, ignore the beaten path and head west instead.

You'll eventually find Grandport Harbor and, just east of it, the Oblivion Palace .

Talk to the Enigmatic Princess, and she will task you with finding the Tablet Shards. Once you return the shards to her, she will open chests based on how many you have delivered.

Increases potency of healing magic by 10%.

Adds a 15% chance of evading magic attacks.

Grants constant Protect when at less than half of max HP.

Increases the duration of debuffs and status ailments inflicted by the wielder by 1 turn.

Increases damage dealt by physical attacks by 10%.

Adds a 15% chance of evading physical attacks.

Restores 5% of max MP upon staggering an enemy.

Imbues non-elemental physical attacks with Light.

articles.summary: Summons, Aeons, Guardian Forces, or Eikons, no matter the moniker, Final Fantasy has always featured majestic, mythical creatures that aid us in battle or give
articles.body:
Summons, Aeons, Guardian Forces, or Eikons, no matter the moniker, Final Fantasy has always featured majestic, mythical creatures that aid us in battle or give us a headache as a challenge. Final Fantasy Resonance features Espers, and they offer us their help by being summonable in battle by Fina, as long as you prove your mettle against them, by strength or intelligence.

After finding your first one, the game teaches you about Espers. However, outside of Siren, all other Espers are optional, so it's up to you to encounter them and harness their power. This IGN guide lists all the Esper locations in Final Fantasy Resonance in order, so you can use this page as a walkthrough as you play.

All Esper Locations in Final Fantasy Resonance

There are 9 Espers to find in Final Fantasy Resonance, as listed below in order and at the earliest possible opportunity to obtain them. If you're missing one, just click on its name below to jump to its exact location.

There is one Esper to find in Chapter 1:

Siren is the first Esper you encounter. She is automatically added to your team during the Chapter 1: Tailing the Truth main story quest .

Note: After obtaining Siren, you can speak to an NPC near the Inn at Grandport Harbor to learn about Esper's rumors and the dwelling of one in the desert. Don't fret about this for now, because you'll only be able to get it in Chapter 4.

Chapter 2 is home to one Esper you can add to your team:

Once you enter Dilmagia, talk to the girl on the right side of the entrance. She'll mention a rumor about a thunderous Esper (we all know who) and mark your map with his dwelling.

Proceed with the main story until you reach Mt. Thunderclap. After you cross it and return to the world map, the game will tell you to go to the Dwarven Forge. On your way to the city, you'll spot a sign. Go east from the sign to return to Mt. Thunderclap. Roll along this path to find a save point and a tombstone at the end. Interact with it to face Ramuh.

He'll ask you a riddle, and while the correct answer is "it's terrifying," there's no wrong one. We suggest choosing the others first to get more of this amusing dialogue. You'll face Ramuh and upon victory, he will be yours to summon.

There is one Esper to find and recruit in Chapter 3:

When you regain control at the beginning of Chapter 3, you'll be by the beach. To the northwest is a Sanctum, and a little past it is the Ruby Cave. Go inside and interact with a stele to read a riddle that lists directions around Olderion.

Outside of Olderion, go east, then south once you reach the sign, and go a tad west to find a sparkling spot between two lakes. Interact with it to pick up your first Ruby Fragment.

Now head back north to where the sign is and go east. Instead of going up the slope that leads you to the Water Cave, stay on the ground level and keep going east until you hit the coast and have to turn north. Pick up the sparkling item on the ground to get your second Ruby Fragment.

Head back to Olderion, and this time go west until you reach the seven waterfalls. Cross one more bridge to the west and grab the third Ruby Fragment on the high ground. Now head back to the Ruby Cave, interact with the stele, and face Levi... oh, wait, it's Carbuncle. You don't have to face it to earn the Summon. Now the rubies make sense.

There are one Esper to befriend in Chapter 4:

You can learn about this Titan's dwelling during Chapter 1, but you can't interact with it until Chapter 4. Once you reach Zoldaad, the Imperial Capital, you can read the bulletin board to learn that the Grandshelt Colosseum has reopened. If you fancy some bouts, you can go there to challenge the Fledgling League and earn some rewards in the process.

The reward for winning the Fledgling Battle 5 is the Gaia Hammer, a weapon for Lid, and also a clue about our mysterious Esper in the desert. With the Gaia Hammer in hand, you can then go to the Grand Shell Desert, east of Grandport Harbor, and smash the seal to liberate Titan.

The colossus will thank you and, as a reward, offer you the chance to be broken to smithereens by his ginormous hands. If you manage to beat Titan, you'll get him as a summon.

Chapter 5 will bolster your forces with 3 more Espers:

From Chapter 5 on, we have an airship to call ours, which means world exploration is open. To keep this guide in order, we will tackle objectives by their in-game recommended level, while still prioritizing side content over the main story.

The male researcher in Zoldaad's inn can tell you the Esper's Dwelling location during Chapter 4, but you won't reach it without the airship you get at the start of Chapter 5. Once you do get the airship, fly into the volcano, interact with it, and enter when the option appears.

Surprise, surprise, a fight awaits you. As the Esper of Fire, Ifrit is immune to Fire, but weak against Water. So bring in Water-aspected Visions and/or Nichol, and douse his burning manes. Upon victory, the flames of hellfire will be at your beck and call.

For the pacifier among you, rejoice: there's no fighting involved this time. All you have to do is go to Olderion and accept the Nichol's Duty sub quest. Once you do, talk to another NPC still in Olderion, and then go to Lake Dorr.

Your next goal is on the World Map, southeast of Olderion. You'll engage with a sahagin, which is a pretty lousy fighter. Once you triumph over them, go to the Cave of Waters entrance, engage with the sahagin once again, and discover the mystery behind everything. The final destination is Lake Dorr once again, where the mighty Leviathan will offer her helping fins as Fina's watery Esper.

Mysidia is harder to find than Shiva. Once you reach Mysidia and are allowed to gallivant through the continent, notice a small island to the southwest. If you talk to an NPC inside the Village of Sunioo's inn, he'll give you the dwelling of our ice queen.

An ice whirlwind swirls on the island, and if you approach it, you can duel Shiva. If you're caught by surprise, you can decline the duel, prepare, and then run back into the whirlwind. Shiva will become your friend after winning the battle.

You can start Odin's quest, the Iron Splitter, in Gronoa. The sub quest becomes available after you conclude the events at the Research Center Ruins and return to Gaberada, where Fina will learn Holy. Once she learns Holy, dispel the miasma and then go all the way east of the continent to find the Bladerain Stele cave. Inside the cave, interact with the stele to initiate the sub quest.

Then continue the main story, advancing through the Rugged Mountain Path. When you wake up in the Town of Duggle, start heading toward the Gronoa Shrine. When you reach a crossroads with a sign, go south, then take the miasma path all the way north to find another stele. Once you interact with it, it will invite you to a mettle demonstration. On your victory, you get the Broken Sword Blade.

Now, fast travel to the Nameless Ruins, south of Mysidia. Teleport to the second save point and enter the north room to find an NPC. Interact with the NPC, and when the cutscene ends, Odin will be yours to summon.

The last Esper, and the best one, resides in Chapter 7.

Sometime during the start of Chapter 7, once you get back in the Airship, a cutscene will occur where both Finas discuss hearing the voice of the Esper Lord of the Heavens. Then, they will tell you to talk to Evan if you want to pursue the voice. As soon as you accept, the battle against Bahamut will ensue.

Bahamut is not only strong, but the mad dragon can apply a bunch of ailments and debuffs to all your characters. It's a pretty daunting battle if you come unprepared, something we think you'll do on your first try. The recommended level is also 50, so we suggest battling only after you've acquired your main party members' Adamantite Weapons and leveled a bunch of Visions, especially Ayaka.

After you defeat Bahamut, and if you have found every other Esper, you'll get the trophy/achievement The Sovereigns of the Planet .

Up Next: How to Beat Ramuh Esper - Boss Guide

articles.title: All Magicite Locations - Final Fantasy Resonance Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Every time you acquire a new Vision in Final Fantasy Resonance and equip it, one of your party members will be able to use that Vision's ability. However,
articles.body:
Every time you acquire a new Vision in Final Fantasy Resonance and equip it, one of your party members will be able to use that Vision's ability. However, you'll notice that every Vision starts at Awakening Level 0, and it's up to you to level them up if you want to unlock stronger abilities.

The way to increase a Vision's Awakening Level is by spending Magicite , a currency found across the world through exploration, by defeating unique enemies, or as subquest rewards. Since there are 26 Visions in total and each one has 3 Awakening Levels, expect to find plenty of Magicite on your journey. This guide will help you find every Magicite in Final Fantasy Resonance so you can awaken your Visions to the max.

All Magicite Locations in Final Fantasy Resonance

There are three types of Magicite in Final Fantasy Resonance: Magicite Shards, Magicite, and Magicite Crysts . Each one upgrades a higher tier of Awakening Level, from 1 to 3, respectively. However, you decide which Visions you want to level up at any given time, as long as you have the resources in hand.

It's not possible to track each individual Magicite in-game, so if you happen to miss any, you'll need to scour every one to see which you haven't picked up yet. That's why we recommend keeping this guide open as you progress through your playthrough.

Upon arriving in the Town of Felicitas, head to the item shop and talk to Charlotte to receive the Secrets Unearthed subquest. Completing it will earn you your very first Magicite Shard.

A reward from gathering 9 Tablet Shards and giving them to the princess at the Oblivion Palace. You can get this many Tablet Shards still in Chapter 1. Use our guide if you're missing any Tablet Shard.

Reward for defeating the main story boss, Tap to Reveal .

Automatically acquired with the Magicite's tutorial.

Reward for completing the Rear Support, Ahoy! sub quest. The sub quest becomes available once you finish Siren's Tower and simply asks you to kill 4 Man Traps around Grandport.

One of the ways to get Magicite is by defeating optional bosses. The first one is the Marauder inside the Marauder's Cave, east of Siren's Tower. The recommended level is 15, which was the level we managed to defeat it at while playing on Expert difficulty.

The Marauder is weak only to Wind, and at this point in the game, you don't have access to Aero through any of your Visions or characters. You can either wait to face it until you get Tap to Reveal or simply win through brute force. One good strategy is to summon Siren every time possible because her final skill, Lunatic Voice, is Wind-aspected and will deal tons of damage.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Marauder page.

Magicite Shard 7 - Dilmagia, the Machinopolis

Reward for completing the Elven Maven sub quest. You can start this quest in Dilmagia and complete it once you explore Mt. Thunderclap.

On Mt. Thunderclap, don't take the easy-peasy shortcut offered by Lid. Go through the normal path and you'll soon find a beige tree. Interact with it, head back to Silvia, and then meet her at the Dwarven Forge next to complete the sub quest.

Return to the world map from Dwarven Forge and go all the way east, past the Sanctum of Zidane. You'll encounter a second entrance to Mt. Thunderclap.

Inside the mountain, run along until you find a save point and a tombstone. If you interact with the tombstone, you'll face Ramuh. Upon victory, you get the thunderous sage as a summon and a Magicite Shard as loot.

Reward for delivering 24 Tablet Shards to the princess at the Oblivion Palace. You can get this many Tablet Shards after finishing the Mobliz Shipyard.

Complete the Arise, Mechabo! sub quest that the game automatically gives to you. Just kill two Ipoohs, and that's it.

Talk to the spoony bard Roy in Dwarven Forge to accept the Lyrical Riddles sub quest. Interact with the quest marker on the Mobliz Shipyard, Dilmagia, then back to Roy and voilá.

In the Wind Shrine, you'll have to call down elevators to proceed. The first is by the entrance, and the second is after traversing via a moving platform. After you take the second elevator, before hopping on the next platform, go south, climb down a set of stairs, and find a chest containing this Magicite Shard.

You can access the Shoggoth Cave by starting at the Wind Shrine, going all the way south, passing under three bridges, then going east at an intersection and staying on this path until you hit the cave. Or, you can wait for the bridge north of Dilmagia to be fixed by the end of Chapter 2.

We suggest the bridge path because it's closer, and by the time it's fixed, you'll be stronger. Shoggoth may seem tricky because it's immune to physical damage, but its magic resistance is quite low. Since it's weak against Earth and Water, bring Terra and the Onion Knight. Upon victory, you'll get a brand-new Magicite Shard.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Shoggoth page.

Magicite Shard 14 - Olderion, the Aquapolis

Once you enter Olderion, go west to find some lovely girls playing jump rope. Challenge them, and if you manage 10 jumps, you get a Magicite Shard as a reward, along with some Final Fantasy IX post-traumatic memories.

While riding the boat, stop by the nearby chest to grab this Magicite Shard.

The Rukh Cave is located just south of Olderion. The monster may have the highest HP of any other you've faced so far, so prepare to spend some Ethers. It deals mostly both magical and physical damage, so you can try to apply Blind/Sleep/Silence whenever possible. It's weak to Aero, so Firion, Zidane and the Onion Knight are good Visions to bring.

Nichol may be a good party member because his Formation can increase everyone's defense to mitigate the enemy's skills, and he can cast Dispel when the Rukh uses Mighty Guard. It's not really mandatory, though, because most of your party flexibility comes from Visions. It can also Petrify and Paralyze your members, so if you have Jeweled Gem accessories, you'd better equip them.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Rukh page.

Magicite Shard 17 - Olderion, the Aquapolis

A reward for completing the Medicinal Mission sub quest, available after finishing the Cave of Waters events. After you get the quest and talk to the apothecary Ilias, he will teach you three ways to get the remedy.

The first way is to defeat the monster Blood Dragon, south of Olderion. The dragon is level 28, weak to fire, has constant regen, and uses area-of-effect water attacks. It's quite challenging, but if you stagger it and dish out Fire damage, it may fall before your Resonance animation ends.

The second way is to get two items, easily done by following their map markers. One is on the world map, south of the Sanctum of Firion, and the other is in the Cave of Waters. This is the recommended way if you don't mind the legwork and prefer to avoid a tough fight.

The third way, and the less recommended one, is to buy the item from a merchant at the Secluded Dwelling west of Olderion. The remedy costs 50,000 Gil, so it's really not worth the price.

Dropped after defeating the main story boss, Tap to Reveal .

Start the The Tide from the Sky sub quest in the Town of Amore to receive a Magicite Shard as a reward. You just need to face some pirates northeast of Amore, and then talk to Mercedes in the Waterfall Way to complete the quest.

You can find the Mindflayer Cave west of the Town of Amore's northern exit. The monster is accompanied by two Mind Elementals who unleash Blizzara upon defeat. The Mindflayer can apply Paralysis, Poison, and Silence to one party member with the devastating attack Mind Blast, and Blind to everyone with Flash, which can be quite annoying.

As a main Earth user, Lid is a good pick for your team, but you can always rely on the Warrior of Light or the Onion Knight to throw rocks at your enemy. If you're feeling adventurous, you can summon Carbuncle, preferably after a Mind Blast. Carbuncle's first spell will cast Reflect on the entire party, which will in turn reflect all of Mindflayer's advances. Just remember that any Cure will also be reflected.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Mindflayer page.

As soon as you board the boat, go straight north and enter a passage in the waterfall to reach a chest.

Reward for delivering 40 Tablet Shards to the princess at the Oblivion Palace. You can get this many Tablet Shard during the Water Shrine dungeon.

Magicite Shard 21 - Grandshelt Colosseum

Once you reach Zoldaad, the bulletin board reads that the Grandshelt colosseum has reopened. You can access the colosseum from the western side of Grandshelt's plaza. The Fledgling League is open, and if you win the first battle, you earn a Magicite Shard. The enemies are common encounters found around Zoldaad.

Magicite Shard 22 - Grandshelt Colosseum

If you're on a streak in the colosseum, you can win Fledgling Battle 4 to net another Magicite. The battle is a bit trickier, but pretty manageable at the recommended level of 31. Two enemies are weak to Fire, and one is weak to Water.

After winning the Fledgling League, you will receive the Fledgling's Proof of Victory , which will expand the shop's inventory. The item shop will start selling Magicite Shards for 10,000 Gil each. If you have followed the guide up to this point, you should already have a surplus of Magicite Shards, so we don't recommend buying any.

Once you reach Zoldaad, the Imperial Capital, the colosseum back at Grandshelt will be reopened. The reward for winning the Fledgling League is the Gaia Hammer, which you can use to unbreak the seal in the Grandshelt Desert to free Tap to Reveal .

If you manage to win against the boss, you not only get him as a summon to help put enemies between a rock and a hard place - his words - but you also earn a Magicite as a drop upon victory.

As you proceed along the Underground Tunnel, you'll eventually go down the iron platform stairs and spot a Magic Pot. Once you reach the pot, look to its right, under the platform, for a chest containing this Magicite Shard.

The Gogmagog Cave is just south of the Rebel Hideout. This giant is a doofus just like it looks, and will mostly employ physical attacks, either against one ally or against the whole party with Thwack, so having Protectga up at all times is a good strategy. Gogmagog will occasionally cast Stonera, but the damage is relatively low. The cave monster is susceptible to Sleep and Blind, which can help mitigate damage.

Since it's weak to Light and Wind, bring Fina for her healing and spells. Vision Cecil can tank damage and deal Light attacks between turns, and Firion has his Light-aspected Resonance. If Firion is at Awakening Level 2, he has the amazing Light ability, Saber of Adversity. For Wind, the Onion Knight and Zidane are good as usual.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Gogmagog page.

You can start the Mechabo Evolved sub quest in Chapter 2, but you won't complete it until Chapter 4, so no Magicite until then. This chain quest asks you to kill increasingly stronger monsters. First, you need to kill Dhorme Chimeras, then Medusaes, then Destroyers, and finally Sandworms. The game will mark the location of these rare monsters, so follow it to get the items you need.

Mechabo will not only become stronger than a red chocobo mounting another red chocobo, but you'll earn a Magicite in the process.

Remember those lovely girls jumping rope? There's a new record to break. If you manage to jump 60 times, which is quite tricky because the rope speed is erratic, you will get a Magicite as a reward.

From the entrance, head up the ladder to the left of the save point. Walk right, and you'll see three switches. Hit the first switch twice, and the second three times. Then cross the platforms to reach the northwesternmost chest and find a Magicite inside.

You can fight the Pyroviper in its cave, south of the Weapons Factory. As expected, the Pyroviper is weak against Water and immune to Fire. One strategy is to equip Azure Amulet on Jake and unleash his non-elemental physical attacks imbued with Water. This will deal some nasty damage to the enemy.

Nichol naturally has Water spells and is always useful with his buffs. You can bring in Visions like Cloud, Terra, and Shantotto to drown the monster with even more Water abilities for the remaining members.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Pyroviper page.

From Chapter 5 on, we have an airship to call ours, which means world exploration is open. To keep this guide in order, we will tackle objectives by their in-game recommended level, while still prioritizing side content over the main story.

Magicite 9 - Zoldaad, the Imperial Capital

At the start of Chapter 5, go to Zoldaad's Residential District and talk to the NPC to start the subquest The Call from Beyond. The reward is a Magicite. Go to the sub quest marker south of the Weapons Factory to be transported to a new zone.

The quest is fairly linear and easy to complete. All you have to do is talk to NPCs, answer some questions (don't worry about getting them wrong at first), and then face a monster by the end. The monster is weak against Light and Ice, for those asking. After you win, the quest will be complete, granting you a Magicite and Camille, a new Vision.

In the Rebel Hideout, talk to Simon to start the Rogue Rebel sub quest. Back in Zoldaad, talk to an NPC in the Imperial Hotel area, then go to the slums, talk to a boy, and then examine the manhole. Travel across the capital and investigate every manhole you can.

Return to the Commercial District, talk to the robed NPC near a cart, and answer "Wild Rose." Give the letter to Simon at the Rebel Hideout to complete the sub quest.

Magicite Cryst 1 - Zoldaad, the Imperial Capital

Must complete The Call from Beyond sub quest first.

Travel to Zoldaad's castle plaza and talk to Ozetta to accept the O General! My General! sub quest. You need to examine two camps, one near the Sanctum of Shantotto and another south of the Weapons Factory, reachable only by air. Once you do, return to the Castle Plaza and talk to Ozetta again.

Your next destination is the Weapons Factory. Once inside, go north from the save point and interact with the marker. Back in Zoldaad, talk to Foxie inside the inn to complete the sub quest and earn your first Magicite Cryst, along with a new Vision: Wilhelm.

You earn this Magicite by defeating Tap to Reveal .

You can fight the flame lord by flying your airship directly into the volcano.

Magicite Shard 24 - Dirnado, the Continent of Wind

Fly your airship west of Dilmagia, past the Sanctum of the Onion Knight, and land in the greenery to find this Magicite Shard in the ground.

Magicite 12 - Dilmagia, the Machinopolis

Enter Dilmagia and accept the sub quest Forger of Wills from the NPC just in front of the entrance. You'll do some legwork at first, talking to Aileen at Dilmagia's shipyard, then with an NPC near Dilmagia's weapon shop, another one in the Rebel Hideout, and one more back in the Town of Kol.

Return to Aileen at the shipyard and answer three questions:

You're done! Aileen will join you as a Vision, bringing with her a Magicite.

The continent on the westernmost side of the world is called Kingdom of Pharm. Fly over there and grab this sparkling on the ground for a Magicite Shard.

In Mysidia, you can play tag with some moogles on the east side of the town. The first game grants you a Mist X-Potion and the second, title More Mog Tag, a Magicite. Here's where you can find them:

One Moogle on the platform by the city entrance

Another in the grave area east of the Potion Factory

Last Moogle in the central area by the pool.

Magicite Cryst 2 - Mysidia, the Magiapolis

Once again, talk to the moogles to start the Even More Mog Tag sub quest. This time the moogles are on Haste, but it's still relatively simple. Here's where you can tag them:

The second is by the bridge west of the Potion Factory

The third is behind the Potion Factory, accessible by entering the portal to the right of the building

Upon completion, a rare and precious Magicite Cryst. It pays to be joyful with moogles.

Start the Mechabo Unleashed sub quest by talking to Verun in Dwarven Forge after reaching Mysidia. Then, talk to the blacksmith back at your Airship's bridge. You know the drill, time to kill some rare monsters.

First order of the day: defeat three mahadevas on an island west of Mysidia. Once you do, return to Verun, learn Overclock Zero for Lid, then head to your next objective: kill three malbodooms in Gronoa. The thing is, you can't go to Gronoa yet. Yet, you can still complete the quest. There's an island before Gronoa, west of the Sanctum of the Onion Knight, where malbodooms spawn. They are level 40, so be careful. However, you can still defeat three of them, complete the quest early, and get another rare Magicite Cryst. Plus, a brand-new Mechabo ability!

Magicite 14 - Mysidia, the Uncharted Land

This Magicite drops when you defeat Tap to Reveal . You'll find her on an island southwest of Mysidia.

Approach the ice whirlwind to trigger the battle.

After visiting the Village of Sunioo, a new sub quest, Victoria Revivified, will unlock back in Mysidia. It's pretty straightforward. First, talk to Victoria, then go to the Potion Factory, interact with her again, and then leave Mysidia. Go towards Victoria's Shrine, west of Mysidia, near the Sanctum of Vaan.

Inside, she will ask you to hunt some enemies on an island northeast of Mysidia. You'll fight three level 35 black lizards that are weak to Ice. They can cast Graviga and Petrify, but they are fairly weak. Defeat them, go to Mysidia's central pool area, sprinkle the powder, and you're done with the sub quest.

Inside a chest to the west of the second save point.

A reward from gathering 64 Tablet Shards and giving them to the princess at the Oblivion Palace. You can get this many Tablet Shards after completing the Nameless Ruins, in case you're using our Tablet Shards guide.

Salome Cave is found southeast of Mysidia, near the Sanctum of Lightning. First things first, you must equip some Charm protection accessories. You can buy Monk's Prayer Beads at Grandport Harbor. Salome will constantly spam Allure, trying to charm your entire party, and then proceed to spam Stonega. Without Charm protection, the battle will be unprecedentedly annoying, even if you manage to win.

Since Salome is weak against Wind, bring in a few Wind-aspected Visions. At this point in the game, you have plenty of options, so go nuts. Our strategy was to use Bartz because he not only increases the Stagger dealt to the enemy, but he can imbue Wind into a character's basic attack, throwing two birds with one stone. Or something.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Salome page.

Magicite 18 - Zoldaad, the Imperial Capital

You earn this Magicite by completing Errand's End sub quest. However, this quest unlocks only after completing The Token Legacy, a subquest that automatically starts after you sleep at a random inn, except the Airship.

The Token Legacy triggered for us after delivering the potions to the Village of Sunioo. Once we completed it, the Errand's End popped up at Zoldaad's bulletin board. Both quests are just legwork, so follow the markers, and you will be done shortly.

While climbing the stairs, you'll reach a snowy outer ring. Go all the way east to find a chest hidden behind the column.

Jotunn will mainly attack with physical attacks against one enemy. One attack can cause Paralyze, another will cast Bravery on the monster, and one is a serious damage. Occasionally, it will cast Blizzaga, which can cause pretty serious damage.

Jotunn's biggest strength is their health. Even if you strike their Fire or Dark weaknesses with Visions, it will still take a while to topple Jotunn because of its massive HP. They also attack twice per turn, so protect your party members accordingly.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Jotunn page.

Once you reach Gaberada, the Undertown, go behind the inn to find a hidden staircase and talk to an NPC, who will give you a Magi-tenna. Give the Magi-tenna to Lid at the Airship, and she will upgrade the radar, allowing you to hunt for treasures around the world.

This Magicite can be found by using the radar in the Zoldaad Empire Territory, just south of Shantottto's Sanctum.

Must complete Elven Maven and Lyrical Riddles sub quests first.

In Gaberada, talk to Fryevia to start "Reunion," her sub quest. Travel to the village of Sunioo and interact with a rosé tree in the northmost part of the village, right of the item shop. NExt, go to Mt. Thudnerclap, and interact with the beige tree. Once done, pay a visit to Dwarven Forge and talk to Silvia.

After teleporting a bunch of times in the room accessible with the level 2 card, you'll climb a ladder to some girders. Once up, go left, down, then right to find a chest with this Magicite.

First-time reward for winning the Brawler Battle 1 at the Colosseum.

Magicite Cryst 5 - Gronoa, the Uncharted Land

This Magicite Cryst is loot for defeating Tap to Reveal . To fight him, you need to start the Iron Splitter sub quest, available after dispelling the miasma in Gronoa.

All you have to do is go all the way east, interact with the steele inside the Bladerain Stele, then proceed with the main story until you reach the Gronoa Shrine.

Instead of going to the shrine, go south of the Rugged Mountain Path exit and keep going along the miasma path until you reach another steele. Win the fight, win the Magicite Cryst.

The second room in the Gronoa Shrine has stairs on both sides. Take the west stairs to proceed. Once you climb down, go west again to find a chest with this Magicite Cryst.

Loot for defeating the dragon. Talk about creative naming.

At the start of Chapter 7, go to Grandport Harbor to begin The Shield of the Weak sub quest. Your first stop is back at Grandshelt Castle, where you need to interact with three markers. Then, go to Kolobos Ruins. From the entrance, go to the next area and talk to some NPCs. You'll enter an easy battle against a Magitek Weapon and three knights.

Your next destination is the Cavern of Swords, located near the Sanctum of Cloud, in the desert northeast of Grandport Harbor. Inside the cavern, talk to Mother and face another Magitek Weapon, slightly stronger than before but still puny. Upon victory, return to Grandshelt Castle, talk to Charlotte, and the sub quest is done, earning you a Vision and another Magicite Cryst as prizes.

After you meet Ayaka in the Town of Sian, she will offer a sub quest when you talk to her again. Titled The Admirable Apprentice, you have to visit a bunch of past dungeons. It's pretty straightforward. Just interact with the markers, kill a level 47 monster weak to Fire and Light, then talk to Ayaka again back in Sian when all is said and done.

Not only will you get a Magicite Cryst, but you'll finally have a new Medic Vision, the best one in our opinion.

You can access the Malboro Varietas Cave as soon as Chapter 5 with the Airship. It's located northeast of the WAter Shrine. However, since the recommended level is 45, we waited until we reached a dungeon with a similar level range.

If you're familiar with Malboros in Final Fantasy, then you know what's awaiting you. Malboro Varietas' devastating attack is Bad Breath, which can apply a bunch of ailments to your characters. Sometimes it hits only 2 characters, but usually it hits more. If you've already concluded Chapter 5, you have a Ribbon accessory. You can also equip Terra at max Awakening Level. Since the monster is weak against fire, burn it to a crisp.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Malboro Varietas page.

First-time reward for winning Brawler Battle 4. You fight five Flan Princesses, who start the fight by casting Berserk in the entire party. They are absorb every element, so you'll ahve to rely on physical attacks. We made short work of them using Double Action and Mecha Behemoth with Lid.

With this, you've earned all Magicites needed to Awaken your Visions to level 2.

From the entrance, you'll cross two bridges. Once you cross the second one, keep going east, up a slope, cross another bridge, and open a chest to find this Cryst.

During your expedition in Mt. Reizan, you'll come across a Resonance Stone. Give it to Lid to further upgrade the radar and unlock more treasure hunting. You can find a Magicite Cryst near Grandshelt. However, you must get the Ancient Hammer first, since you have to do treasure hunting in order.

Check our Treasure Hunting guide if you want to find every item effortlessly.

In Gabareda, the Undertown, if you talked to some NPCs, you may have heard about a Merchant Ship selling wares sporadically throughout the world. We believe the ship its wares at different stages of the game, and the items are ordered.

If you start looking for the Merchant Ship early on, you'll find Ancient weapons, an Adamantite, and eventually a Magicite Cryst. We got this Magicite Cryst by finding the Merchant Ship in the seas between the Mozul Station and the Kolobos Ruins, just before the Wandering Lands. If you want guidance on where to find the Merchant Ship, check our Equipment guide page.

There's a Whirlpool Hollow between the Grandshelt Castle continent and Grandport Harbor that you can access via the Airship starting Chapter 5. There, you'll encounter the Will of the Light and a challenge against a level 45 boss. If you win, you'll get Tap to Reveal , plus a Magicite Cryst.

We have no doubt you can challenge yourself and triumph against the boss well before Chapter 7, but we waited until our level was around what the main story recommended to improve our fighting chance.

The Tartarosaurus Cave is on an island northeast of Mysidia. Since its recommended level is above the previous boss, the dino has substantially more HP. Yet, if you managed to defeat the above, the Tartarosaurus is going to be a walk in the park.

He mostly deals physical attacks, so focus on Protecting your party and use Ice abilities. It may take a while, but you will defeat it eventually and net one more Magicite Cryst for the team.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Tartarosaurus page.

At the start of Chapter 7, a cutscene will occur once you enter the Airship's bridge where Fina will discuss hearing the voice of an Esper. Then, they will tell you to talk to Evan if you want to pursue the voice. As soon as you accept, the battle against Tap to Reveal will ensue.

The battle can be quite hard at the start of Chapter 7 because the recommended level is 50, which is why we've only included this Magicite Cryst after the optional level 45 boss and the Tartarosaurus Cave. On your victory, you get a new Esper and one more Magicite Cryst.

The next time you find the Merchant Ship, in the middle of the ocean southeast of the Gronoa continent, it will be selling a High-Power Generator for 60,000 gil to upgrade your radar further. Buy it, give it to Lid, and then search for this Magicite Cryst in the far south of the ocean.

The Catacumba Cave is on an island between Gronoa and the Kingdom of Pharm. By this point, you've already found an almighty team build you'll use until the end, killing enemies in just a few turns.

Catacumba is relatively easy compared to the last Vision you'll get, or the Chamber of Arms bosses, even though the recommended level is higher. Your go-to strategy is to focus on its weaknesses and chip away at its HP little by little.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Catacumba page.

You can find the Necromonarch Cave near the Town of Duggle, before you get to the Gronoa Shrine. The Necromonarch is also weak to Light and Fire, like the previous enemy, but it counters Magic attacks, so focus on Physical.

There's not much secret here. Just overwhelm it with your best abilities, and it will soon die. Since it's an undead, healing magic also works.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Necromonarch page.

The Humbaba Cave is on the far west side of the Gronoa continent. You can fast travel to the Research Center Ruins or the Bladestele Cave, then proceed to the cave.

Humbaba is weak to Wind and can apply debuffs like Paralysis, Blind, Confuse, and Berserk. You can safeguard each party member, or equip Ribbon on one character and place an Esunaga-owned Vision on them. Or you can focus on an overwhelming offensive build and defeat Humbaba before it can apply any ailments.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Humbaba page.

Some Magicites in Chapter 8 are found in the post-game, because the recommended level for some content is higher than the last dungeon. We will list the acquisition order by required level.

Magicite Cryst 20 - Grandshelt Colosseum

First-time reward for winning Gladiator Battle 1.

Inside a chest beside the last save point.

Dropped after winning against Tap to Reveal and Tap to Reveal .

Proceed through Dragon's Maw normally until you reach the second save point. Backtrack a bit, take the northwestern slope down, and keep going until you reach a chest with this Cryst.

The Malboro Menace Cave is located in the north region of the Kingdom of Pharm and is easily reachable via Airship. Be prepared, because this is the worst kind of Malboro, the one every Final Fantasy player has nightmares about. The monster's first attack is Putrid Breath, which applies a ludicrous amount of ailments to all allies. If you don't have a Ribbon equipped, just restart the fight.

Once you deal with the ailments, preferably via an Esunaga to the same ally protected with Ribbon, you should start using Fire attacks against the boss or just any kind of attacks. Other than the Putrid Breath, the Malboro Menace doesn't have any major attacks.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Malboro Menace page.

The Titanoraidos Cave is sneakily tuked away in the Kingdom of Pharm, west of Mt. Reizan entrance. The enemy is failry resistant and gets stronger the longer the battle drags out. Titanoraidos can also remove a target from battle using one of its skills.

However, since it's an endgame Cave Monster, and probably the last one you'll face, you must have be already armed every single party member with Guns Akimbo, Double Aciton, Dual Cast and any skills that allow you to act 20 times before the enemy even gets a turn, so just do your thing and it's allright.

For a more detailed strategy and fight walkthrough, head over to our How to Beat Titanoraidos page.

Magicite Cryst 26 - Grandshelt Colosseum

articles.summary: Visions are the unique mechanic that sets Final Fantasy Resonance apart from Square Enix's other recent turn based titles. These past Final Fantasy
articles.body:
Visions are the unique mechanic that sets Final Fantasy Resonance apart from Square Enix's other recent turn based titles. These past Final Fantasy protagonists can be equipped to your party to impart stat boosts, special passives, and powerful attacks. But which past hero is the strongest of them all? This IGN guide will detail each of the Visions in Final Fantasy Resonance, and explains which ones will help you build the strongest party possible.

If you are looking for a tl;dr, here is a quick list of Visions to level up as soon as you get them:

Rain is a fierce hero who loves to protect others. His Provoke skill, which causes enemies to focus on him rather than his companions, pairs really well with the Warrior of Light’s counter-attacking abilities. Equip items that imbue elements to your basic attacks or Anti-Magic Studs to make Rain counter magic attacks as well and you’ll be making every enemy regret the fact that they dared to come at you.

That said Rain also ranks high among the physical attackers, especially once you get his unique ability, The Power Within, in the late game. His Ultimate Weapon, Ragnarok, increases the power of non-elemental attacks which gives a nice boost when pairing him with Bartz and Flare Blade.

Lasswell is the team’s only Breaker but we have an abundance of fantastic Breaker visions to choose from for his Vision pairing. The strength of a Breaker is their ability to Stagger enemies, so you’ll want to pair him with Bartz who will let you dual attack with his Spellblade skills and wields three elements that pair well with Lasswell to fill coverage gaps and quickly ramp up Stagger, then take this to the next level by equipping the Arms Akimbo, Double Action and Half MP Cost combo for your abilities, filling in the gaps with critical and Stagger buffs from Cloud, Sephiroth and Tronn.

Alternatively, Lasswell also makes for one of the best tanks in the game as well thanks to his insanely high speed and built in dodge on his Ultimate Weapon, Sasuke's Blade. Pair him with Wilhelm or Cecil for HP and Defense boost, then have him using Multi-Cover and Guard to neutralize any threat to your party allowing them to attack freely.

Fina touts the highest Sanctity stat of any party member, and is the only character with a wide array of White Magic built right into her kit. For this reason she doesn't really need the help of a healing Vision like Leah or Ayaka, and instead should be more of a hybrid support. Equip her with Y'Shtola for some extra elemental coverage (Wind and Ice), an extra powerful healing spell, and access to Protectga to go with the Shellga already in her skillset.

Archwitch Fina however can be used to do scaling damage with her dark attacks. She has great synergy with Terra’s magic buffs and the Sharp Mind ability that doubles the damage of multi-target attacks that hit only one enemy, making her main damaging skill Dystopia extremely useful no matter how many enemies are left. She also makes a great combination with Shantotto, whose focus on dark element spells synergises well with Archwitch Fina’s Paradise Lost skill.

Her best pairing though is the difficult to acquire Sephiroth, who passively grants huge buffs to both magic and physical damage, an additional 40% critical hit rate and the ability Legendary Soldier. Legendary Soldier lets Fina use her highest attack stat when attacking and her highest defensive stat when defending. Her ability Queenly Whip, which reduces enemy attack and magic attack, pairs perfectly with Sephiroth's Purging Blade, which reduces enemy defense and magic defense. This combo, and her many weapons that increase debuff duration, make her easily the best debuffer in the game.

Lid is our gadget girl and is centered around a long term questline that progressively grants upgrades to her Mechabo’s combat ability. Lid’s ultimate pairing is Cloud who shares her love of crits and staggering enemies. Lid’s Overclock and Overclock Zero skills provide 150% and 300% boosts respectively to the damage and stagger power of the next 3 Mechabo skills, stacking together for insane damage output but with the caveat that Mechabo can’t use any skills for the next two turns as he cools down. While you wait for Mechabo to be up and ready again you can make use of Cloud’s spellblade attacks and extra coverage.

Nichol is the best support in the game thanks to his high Magic stats and his Tactic: Fluid Warfare skill that lets him take an extra turn every time he uses a Formation buff. Paired with Arms Akimbo, that is 4 actions per turn. Pair him with Leah, Y'Shtola, or Ayaka and suddenly you have the ultimate healer and buff machine all in one. The devs likely intended this, since his Ultimate Weapon, Last Resort, gives him a huge boost to the healing stat, Sanctity.

Any Physical Attacker ( Bartz , Cloud , Noctis , Sephiroth )

Jake is the the game's strongest physical attacker in terms of pure stats, comes with Brave in his base kit, and his various 'Luck' abilities serve to further boost his attack if you can manage them properly. Bartz, Cloud, Noctis, Sephiroth. Any of these physical attack visions will shine on Jake, but also consider Cecil.

Cecil gives boosts to Attack, Defense, and HP, powerful Light and Dark physical attacks, as well as Protectga and Shellga. This will turn Jake into a dual threat buffing and attacking beast.

While Jake can handle the physical side of things, Sakura is a really powerful mage. Terra is probably her most obvious pairing. Terra gives her access to three elements not within her base skillset (as well as Ultima), Break Damage Limit, Passive Ribbon, and a massive boost to Magic Attack. On top of that, Terra's Sharp Mind and Magic Boost abilities boost Sakura's magic attacks even more, going nicely with Sakura's other buffs like Concentrate.

Alternatively, Shantotto is a good time as she can do wild damage to an entire group of enemies, thanks to the ability Area Effect Adept which lets her multicast without damage penalties, and the skill Dualcast that lets her cast black or white magic spells twice in a turn. Shantotto does the most when she's not focusing on staggering, but rather when she's spamming powerful skills like Salvation Scythe. This already large amount of damage increases even more once you awaken her three star ability Play Rough to buff Salvation Scythe even more.

articles.title: Character Tier List - Final Fantasy Resonance - Final Fantasy Resonance Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's guide to the Best Characters in Final Fantasy Resonance. There are 8 party members to choose from, and they are all good in their own
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's guide to the Best Characters in Final Fantasy Resonance. There are 8 party members to choose from, and they are all good in their own ways. For that reason, we will only be ranking them into three tiers to indicate their relative closeness in capabilities.

This IGN guide will offer a quick summary of each characters capabilities and their strengths.

Of course the protagonist is going to be a top tier. Rain is one of the strongest attackers throughout pretty much the entire game, and boasts the highest health and physical defense stats as well. He has Fire attacks by default, but becomes a threat when paired with any physical attacking Vision. In the late game, he also gets a unique skill, The Power Within, that permanently raises all his attributes by 25%.

Nichol sneaks his way into S tier off the strength of just one skill: Tactic: Fluid Warfare. This buff lets him take an extra turn after using one of his Formation skills. Combined with Firion's Arms Akimbo, Nichol can take 4 actions on every one of his turns. This makes him far and away the best and most versatile support in the game.

Sakura is one of the final party members you get, and also the game's premiere Magic Attacker. Her offensive stats are high by default, and she has multiple powerful buffs like Concentrate that increase her magic even further. She has three different elements in her kit by default, and when equipped with any magic attacker her potential and coverage expands even further. She also has an incredible LB1, Eternal Veil, which negates all damage a single time.

In story and in gameplay, Lasswell plays second fiddle to Rain. He excels in pretty much all the same ways, and some of his stats are actually higher, but less health and defense, and no access to a broken buff like The Power Within. However he is the fastest unit in the game (tied with Nichol), which has its own applications when it comes to late game team building.

Jake's skillset revolves around a unique Luck mechanic that expands his arsenal and powers up his attacks. However, he also has the highest physical attack stat of anyone in the game by far (as well as access to the Brave spell) so you can choose to fully ignore the Luck and just pair him with any physical attacking Vision with great success.

Because you get Archwitch Fina so late into the game it can be kind of hard to understand where she fits in the team. She has primarily Dark spells, but also a couple of powerful non-elemental attacks like Meteor and Ultima. Her kit excels at debuffing, and many of her weapons extend the duration of debuffs she inflicts. Her Queenly Whip skill inflicts both Debrave and Defaith all at once, making it one of the best single debuff attacks in the game. As a bonus she can also summon Espers.

Fina will be your support and healer for most of the game thanks to her built in access to a wide variety of White Magic, and the highest Sanctity stat of anyone. She also has a number of a powerful buffs, like Arcane Guard and Cheer. She is a capable magic attacker, and of course she is one of two characters who can summon Espers. However, by the late game she gets quickly outclassed as a healer by Nichol, and an attacker by Archwitch Fina. This leaves Fina without a specialty of her own, outside of casting her unique spells like Cheer and Holy.

Lid is the all around character, and not much else. She has pretty much equal stats in both physical and magic attack, but doesn't excel at any one thing. Her skillset is small, and very Earth focused, and slowly expanded via side quests. She also doesn't have any standout buffs or support skills to offer, other than the useful skill Mechabo Escape for getting out of battles.

articles.title: How to Beat Sephiroth - Location and Guide - Final Fantasy Resonance Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Sephiroth can be found in the Whirlpool Hollow near Grandshelt, as soon as you obtain the Airship. Unlike other Visions you will need to defeat Sephiroth in a
articles.body:
Sephiroth can be found in the Whirlpool Hollow near Grandshelt, as soon as you obtain the Airship. Unlike other Visions you will need to defeat Sephiroth in a battle to obtain him.

This IGN guide teaches you how to find and defeat Sephiroth in Final Fantasy Resonance, including how to prepare for the fight and the best strategy to use to beat the Vision and add him to your team.

Sephiroth's Sanctum is found inside Whirlpool Hollow, which you may have noticed in the water as you left Grandshelt early in the game. Once you have the Airship in Chapter 5 you can fly to the whirlpool and go inside.

Sephiroth has no weaknesses, but using the Mechamog Scan skill (unlocked via the Mechabo Unleashed sidequest) we can give him one, and focus it to optimize damage. You may have to reload the fight repeatedly until you get the weakness you want.

We recommend doing this battle shortly after completing Sanctissimus Shrine, which should put you right around the correct level range and unlocks Rain's handy The Power Within skill.

We recommend the following party: Rain+Bartz, Lid+Tronn, Nichol+Leah/Ayaka, and Sakura+Terra. This gives you both a powerful physical and magical attacker, and the best support in the game in Nichol. Lid is essential for Mechamog Scan, but afterwards she can Pass the Torch her turn to Rain every time.

If you have any Adamantite , be sure to speak to Aileen on the Airship and craft some new weapons. The most useful are Rain's Save the Vermillion and Nichol's Codex of Providence.

You need to be versatile in this battle, so give as many of your party members as possible Leah's Pass the Torch ability. This will let you substitute in a healer turn whenever necessary.

Other essential abilities are: Half MP Cost, Arms Akimbo (+Double Action/Dualcast), Scan and Strike, Reflex, and Spry Steps. Try to have as many of these as possible on every party member.

Nichol and Sakura also come with the added benefit of great LB skills. Nichol's Mirroring Prism doubles every party members actions on their next turn, which can double all attacks. Sakura's LB Eternal Veil can stop one instance of damage, which might save you if things turn bad at any point in the fight.

The final phase of this battle is a damage race to beat an attack that results in an instant team wipe. This is the time to fully upgrade and level up Bartz to gain access to his most powerful attacks and Dual Spellblade.

If you want to practice the full fight, you can always save and switch to Casual mode to see and learn all the phases.

You should be around the Level 50-55 range to take on this fight.

Sephiroth Boss Guide - Best Strategy and Tips

Sephiroth is a Lv. 45 Humanoid with 250,000 health. He has No Weaknesses. You will need the Mechamog Scan ability to most effectively battle him.

Sephiroth is a very strong foe who's relatively low level betrays his true difficulty. You might struggle to defeat him, even when you are well into Level 50+ if you aren't properly prepared. The first step of this preparation should be completing the Mechabo Unleashed sidequest and unlocking the Mechabo Scan ability . If you use Libra on Sephiroth you will notice it advises you to hit his weakness, of which he has none. We can fix this with Mechamog Scan, giving him a weakness and making the battle much more managable.

In Phase 1 Sephiroth uses an ability called Masamune in Waiting that makes him immune to physical attacks, so you need to do about 20% of his health using mostly magic only. We recommend picking a single element you want to focus on, preferably one covered by Bartz (Lightning, Wind, Earth). You may need to reset the fight a few times until you get your chosen element randomly selected by Mechamog Scan. We chose Lightning, then hit Sephiroth with Tronn's Thundaga and Sakura's Tonitus until Phase 1 was over .

Anytime Masamune in Waiting is not active, Rain can contribute a Thundaga Blade as well. Note that when Sephiroth hits the end of a phase, he becomes immune to damage until he can take his next action. If you have party member actions remaining, use this time to buff rather than attack.

At about 80% health Sephiroth buffs himself with "One-Winged Angel", giving him a new set of moves and starting Phase 2 of the battle. Sephiroth becomes stronger, but he also lowers his physical guard allowing you to strike him with all types of attacks. This is where Rain becomes fully unleashed. You will want either Double Action or Arms Akimbo so you can use 4 Spellblade attacks in a single turn. If you happen to have both, you can chain Arms Akimbo into Double Action for 8 Spellblade attacks at once. As mentioned above we set his weakness to Lightning, so we hit him with as many Thundaga Blades as possible . Sakura can continue to use Tonitus, and Lid should begin using Pass the Torch to give her turn to Rain every single time.

At this point Sephiroth will introduce his most dangerous attack, Heartless Angel, which reduces all party members HP to 1 . There is a small chance you will get wiped by this ability with no chance to counter if the turn order goes badly, but this is why we give as many party members as possible Pass the Torch so once you regain control you can always give the turn to Nichol for a double Curaga. DO NOT cast Slow on Sephiroth , as this can push all of his actions to the end of the turn, which greatly increases the chances of him death comboing you.

Sephiroth's other new abilities are Nihilistic Solitude and element Infusion. Nihilistic Solitude is an area attack that removes all buffs. Not very powerful, but annoying as it could be the final thing that takes you out after Heartless Angel (thankfully the debuff effect does not remove The Power Within).

Element Infusion charges Sephiroth with the chosen element, and then releases a Wail of that element on his next turn. Each element inflicts a specific status effect, such as Silence for Wind or Paralysis for Lightning. Because we cannot cover all status effects this is another potential pain point, make sure you equip your Ribbon on Nichol and Max Level Terra on Sakura to at least immunize half your party .

Elemental Infusion also changes Sephiroth's weaknesses and resistances, giving him an immunity to whatever element he is infused with. Thankfully, Mechamog Scan seems to override this effect , so even if he infuses himself with Lightning we can still hit him (note: during elemental infusion he also counters any non-elemental attacks, so don't use any normal attacks or Flare Blade)

If you survive the gauntlet of Phase 2 attacks you should be able to Stagger Sephiroth within two turns of Thundaga Blade barrages. Once he is staggered, damage him down to 20% health at which point he will become immune again in preparation for Phase 3 . Use any extra turns to buff or restore MP if needed. Use Leah's Resonance to full heal.

In Phase 3 Sephiroth's weaknesses change again. He becomes weak to Light, and absorbs Dark. Thankfully the Mechamog Scan still does not reset, so whatever you have been hitting him with you can keep it up.

Phase 3 begins with Sephiroth's ultimate attack, Divine Proclamation. This sets a timer for 8 actions, at which point a Meteor will strike killing your entire party immediately (even blocking skills like Eternal Veil cannot stop it). Thankfully he's only got about 50,000 health left, so that's way more turns than we need. If Nichol has his LB2 charged, unleash it now to give Rain even more Thundaga Blades and Sakura even more Tonitus. That should be more than enough to finish him off.

If not, continue to play safe and heal up, as Sephiroth will likely drop another Heartless Angel on you around this time. With Lid passing her turn to Rain, you should only need 2 more turns to finish him off. This is also as good a time as any to use Sakura's LB1 Eternal Veil if you have it, or burn some powerful healing items. You don't want to lose in the final stretch just for being stingy!

You'll receive the following rewards for defeating Sephiroth in battle:

Defeating him also, of course, earns you the Sephiroth Vision .
